title: Pixel editor within game
author: Nightstar31415
selftext:
This might be a very stupid idea to some, but I got tired of AI messing up some animations and pixels. So I asked it to create an in game pixel editor. If I see something I don't like while implementing a new unit, I go to the menu and fetch the unit. There I can edit the pixels I want, and export a json with the edits. I then give it to Astra to import and update the published web version.

I know there are probably more standard ways to export the graphics, fix in a separate tool etc. But this seemed like a smoother workflow for me. Now I promt astra to create a new unit. I enter the game and inspect it. Edits things I don't like and give Astra the updated version.

comments.author: Blake9712
comments.body:
That’s how I spent the first 3 months on mine, making the asset editor then I make the assets. I eventually had Claude start helping with the assets because it became so exhausting but I make and edit all the levels, items, characters and rooms in my asset editor. It doesn’t look unlike yours really (this is a much earlier version of my game, I don’t have a new video ready)   


https://reddit.com/link/pdh0pg7/video/zq24zkf8u3th1/player

replies.author: Nightstar31415
replies.body: Cool! We had a similar idea for sure. I also thought I could remake all texture by hand, but it's close to 1000 frames for animations for different units now. So probably will never happen. But I can tweak and quality check.

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body: I understand that. On the frames, because mine isn’t pixel art really but instead it’s shapes and layers which is what I’m best at (think early South Park) I can flag stuff to arms and so I don’t have to make all of the sword slash style animations. I was gonna add that to my comment but I realized that may be hard on yours if it’s just pixel art and it can’t easily identify what is an arm ect but maybe you can flag all of the pixels on a limb and have the animations move them instead of manually modeling them? Idk. One tedious thing on mine is just the amount of levels and items I need for the game loop to work. But I’ve been trying to cut down on how much I have to draw.

replies.author: Nightstar31415
replies.body: Indeed, even the ai struggle to identify an arm. If it adds a sword swing, the original arm will stay put. I tried a model where all body parts were connected but thar became messy 😅 World building is actually what I enjoy. So maybe my next game in future should be more reliant on that. (Current game generates world automatically).

replies.author: Blake9712
replies.body:
I see. I wouldn’t really know exactly how your system works but I was wondering if a tool to flag something as an arm, maybe you drag out a square and all objects inside of the square get a flag for arm (or if you utilize elbow I suppose you’re need two arm flags unless it assumes there should be a natural bend at a certain percentage of the length of the arm flagged pixels) would help simplify it but if having connected but separate body parts that probably would too, maybe as the models advance they can take a heavier load. And I like crafting the levels because I can give them themes, ie a football stadium, a few Nintendo and super hero parodies ect but it’s time consuming and I try to add some randomness by having certain enemies have a random weapon, but I really enjoy crafting the levels. Although handcrafting them takes a ton of time but I do like doing it that way because it makes the game feel like it’s mine even if what I hand craft is just a parody half the time lol
